newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam issues death sentences in graft trial.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam issues death sentences in graft trial.

text.p: A court in southern Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City on Friday sentenced four people to death at the end of the communist country's biggest corruption trial.
A court official said that one other defendant had been sentenced to life imprisonment.
Local journalists who attended the case said 15 other defendants were being punished with jail terms, but two of these were suspended.
Despite widespread coverage in the domestic media, foreign journalists were not allowed to attend.
The trial -- a showcase for Hanoi's anti-graft resolve -- centred around allegations of corruption at Ho Chi Minh City firm Tamexco, a trading company affiliated to the ruling Communist Party.

Earlier this week the lead defendants had pleaded for their lives to be spared. Defence lawyers had argued that they were victims of a lax administrative environment in Vietnam which allowed corruption to flourish.
Tamexco director, Pham Huy Phuoc, was named as one of the four people sentenced to death by firing squad.
The others were local company directors Tran Quang Vinh and Le Minh Hai, and the head of a state notary office, Le Duc Canh.
Among those facing jail terms are two former heads of Vietnam's biggest state-owned commercial bank, Vietcombank, and two other banking officials.
The verdicts were largely unchanged from the sentences demanded earlier in the week by state prosecuters, who had also called for investigators to continue probing the case after the trial ended.
Tamexco is a Ho Chi Minh City trading company. Several of those who have been implicated have close links to some of the most powerful people in Vietnam.
